# Kiln

> Kiln is a free, open-source panel for game servers, apps, Docker, and databases, running on machines you own. It is in early development.

Kiln has two parts. Hearth is the web panel. A Relay runs on each machine you own and runs the containers. Everything runs in its own container on a machine you choose, with the same console, files, backups, and access controls.

## What it runs

- Game servers, started from Bricks, such as Minecraft and Palworld. Kiln sets up ports and the right Java version. You can write your own Bricks or add community catalogs.
- Apps, deployed from a GitHub repository, a Docker image, or a Compose file. Kiln builds each push and switches over once the new containers are healthy.
- Databases: MySQL, MariaDB, PostgreSQL, Redis, and Valkey, next to the app or server that uses them.

## Features

- A live console with search across long logs, and a file editor with a file tree, file search, one-click sharing to mclo.gs, NBT editing (such as level.dat), and SQLite editing.
- Backups to S3-compatible storage, schedules, per-instance access control, and an activity history.
- Cloudflare DNS for game server addresses, automatic HTTPS for app domains, Tailscale, a command-line tool, and updates from the panel.

## Compared with other panels

Checked October 2026; the full chart is at https://kiln.site/compare.

- Pterodactyl and AMP are game server panels. Kiln also runs apps from Git and databases in the same panel. Pick Pterodactyl for the most proven option, with a large catalog of extensions, plugins, and eggs. Pick AMP if your servers run on Windows and you want something that works out of the box.
- Coolify, Dokploy, and Openship are app platforms. Kiln covers the same ground for apps and adds game servers. Coolify has the larger catalog of one-click services, and Pterodactyl the larger catalog of game server eggs. Pick Dokploy to shard apps across a Docker Swarm cluster.
- Portainer manages Docker, Swarm, and Kubernetes at the level of containers. Pick it to manage Kubernetes or Swarm directly.
- Kiln has a terminal and file browser on each machine, per-instance permissions, automatic Cloudflare DNS, updates from the panel, and vulnerability scanning of hosts and images. It runs on Linux with Docker, not Windows, and doesn't orchestrate Swarm or Kubernetes.

## Pricing and license

- Self-hosting is free, with no limits. Hosted plans, where Kiln runs Hearth while your machines run everything else, are coming soon.
- Kiln is open source under AGPL-3.0, with a commercial license available.
